author: ORACLE · G9V35-O5
target: Choose and connect a route from the combined system to an individual block; distinguish its net force from its contact force.
entry_message: A contact force and a block's net force can have different values. We will connect the parts and check which force belongs where.
diagnostic_interpretation_note: A selected distractor is a hypothesis, not proof of the route used. Do not diagnose the kid from the Owner's synthetic trial.

worked_case.diagram: 20 N -> [A: 2 kg][B: 3 kg], frictionless horizontal table; blocks remain in contact.
worked_case.question: What contact force does B exert on A?

stages.see: Circle A+B. The 20 N push comes from outside. The contact pair is internal to this combined system.
stages.do: Choose the system you would start with and say what force remains external.
stages.feedback: For A+B the internal contact pair cancels in the combined sum, while the external 20 N push remains.

stages.see: Now isolate B. Its only horizontal force is A's contact force on B.
stages.do: Use the common acceleration to find that contact force.
stages.feedback: For B: C = 3 × 4 = 12 N right. B's reciprocal force on A is 12 N left.

stages.see: Return to A: a 20 N push right and a 12 N contact force left.
stages.do: Choose what 8 N describes: A's net force / A on B contact force / B on A contact force / the whole system's net force.
stages.feedback: A's net force is 20 - 12 = 8 N right = 2 × 4. The contact force is 12 N; the net force is the sum of the forces received by A.

stages.see: Hide the worked equations when you are ready.
stages.do: Explain or reconstruct how you would get the contact force, and why it differs from A's net force. A sentence, sketch description or calculation is welcome. You can also choose 'I cannot explain it yet.'
stages.feedback: Compare with: use A+B to get their common acceleration, then isolate B to get its contact force, then reverse direction for the reciprocal force on A. An equivalent consistent route is valid.
stages.evidence_rule: Save the attempt before comparison. Mark it as guided learning, never independent re-check evidence. No arbitrary text-length gate and no automatic semantic grading.

recheck.stem: A (3 kg, on the left) and B (2 kg, on the right) touch on a frictionless horizontal table. A 35 N horizontal push acts rightward on A and they remain in contact. What contact force does B exert on A?
recheck.expected_reason: For A+B, a=35/(3+2)=7 m/s² right. For B, A's contact force on B=2×7=14 N right; its reciprocal force on A is 14 N left. A's net force is instead 3×7=21 N right. Accept an equivalent consistent route.
recheck.type_rationale: A fresh same-cell problem with a route to choose and dependent system/body steps; no intermediate acceleration, law selection, route menu or hints are supplied.
recheck.level_note: Proposed D1 to match the P1 cell; the non-author must verify type and level before learner use.

A.possible_interpretation: May equate the contact force with the full external push.

B.possible_interpretation: May report the 21 N magnitude of A's net force as its contact force.

D.possible_interpretation: May treat an internal force as zero because its reciprocal pair cancels in a combined sum.

recheck.administration: Capture choice or no_answer, optional reason, confidence and time before feedback. Do not supply a route or hint. If help is requested, submit as not demonstrated before teaching. After the solution has been exposed, repeating this item is practice, not a fresh check.
recheck.result_rule: Show the observed independent answer result and whether a route was recorded. Never auto-declare mastery or promote to D2 from this one item.
